stem: Copper is a transition element. It forms a wide variety of compounds.

parts.label: (b)(i)
parts.stem: An aqueous solution of copper(II) sulfate, $\text{CuSO}_4$, contains $[\text{Cu}(\text{H}_2\text{O})_6]^{2+}$ complex ions. If an excess of concentrated hydrochloric acid is added to this solution a ligand exchange reaction occurs and $[\text{CuCl}_4]^{2-}$ complex ions are formed.
parts.text:
Complete Table 5.1 to state the geometry, the coordination number of copper, and one bond angle in each of the two complex ions.

Table 5.1

| complex ion | geometry | coordination number | bond angle |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| $[\text{Cu}(\text{H}_2\text{O})_6]^{2+}$ |  |  |  |
| $[\text{CuCl}_4]^{2-}$ |  |  |  |

parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.text:
In an isolated $\text{Cu}^{2+}$ ion the d-orbitals are all degenerate. In a complex ion such as $[\text{Cu}(\text{H}_2\text{O})_6]^{2+}$ the d-orbitals are non-degenerate.

Define degenerate and non-degenerate in this context.

parts.label: (b)(iii)
parts.text: Explain why the solutions of the two complex ions in Table 5.1 are **different** colours.

parts.label: (c)(i)
parts.stem: $\text{Cu}^{2+}$ forms a complex ion containing water molecules and ethanedioate ions, $\text{C}_2\text{O}_4^{2-}$, as ligands. The formula of the complex is $[\text{Cu}(\text{C}_2\text{O}_4)_2(\text{H}_2\text{O})_2]^{2-}$. The ethanedioate ion is a bidentate ligand.
parts.text: Explain what is meant by bidentate.

parts.label: (c)(ii)
(c)(iii)
parts.text:
Use your answer to **(c)(ii)** to answer this question.

Stereoisomers 1, 2 and 3 show two different types of isomerism.

Name these two types of isomerism.

For each type of isomerism identify the pair of stereoisomers that demonstrate this isomerism.

| :--- | :--- |

parts.label: (d)
parts.text:
A solution contains $3.70\text{ g}$ of $\text{Na}_2[\text{Cu}(\text{C}_2\text{O}_4)_2(\text{H}_2\text{O})_2]$ dissolved in $100\text{ cm}^3$ of solution. A $25.0\text{ cm}^3$ sample of this solution is warmed and then oxidised by $0.0100\text{ mol dm}^{-3}$ acidified potassium manganate(VII).

The equation for the redox reaction is shown.

$$5\text{C}_2\text{O}_4^{2-} + 2\text{MnO}_4^- + 16\text{H}^+ \rightarrow 10\text{CO}_2 + 2\text{Mn}^{2+} + 8\text{H}_2\text{O}$$

Calculate the minimum volume of $0.0100\text{ mol dm}^{-3}$ acidified potassium manganate(VII) needed to oxidise all of the ethanedioate ions, $\text{C}_2\text{O}_4^{2-}$, in the $25.0\text{ cm}^3$ sample. Show all your working.

[$M_r$: $\text{Na}_2[\text{Cu}(\text{C}_2\text{O}_4)_2(\text{H}_2\text{O})_2]$, 321.5]

parts.label: (e)
parts.text:
Copper(II) nitrate, $\text{Cu}(\text{NO}_3)_2$, and barium nitrate, $\text{Ba}(\text{NO}_3)_2$, both decompose when heated.

Copper(II) nitrate decomposes at a lower temperature than barium nitrate.

Suggest a reason for this difference. Explain your answer.
